title: Post hot-route lane health + throttling spike summaries into incident channels (with runbook links)
author: Rafael Mendes
release_notes: Incident-bot now posts an automated “lane health + throttling spike” summary into active incident channels when hot-route protection signals indicate overload (or when SRE triggers it manually). Message includes links to the throttling dashboard and the on-call runbook, plus guidance on when to page / when to tune alert thresholds during planned load tests.
description: Motivation: During recent capacity dips and retry storms, on-call spent too long triangulating whether enterprise lanes were actually protecting top routes and whether throttling was expected vs symptomatic. This PR adds a lightweight, incident-safe summary message posted by incident-bot into the incident Slack channel when (a) we detect a throttling spike / lane saturation alert, or (b) a responder runs /lane-health. The message includes: enterprise lane health (utilization %, queue depth trend, admission rejection rate), throttling spike details (throttled_count rate, reason code breakdown), top affected routes (redacted / hashed route identifiers for safety), and direct links to the relevant Grafana dashboard and the overload/throttling runbook. This is designed to be explainable to responders and safe under high alert volume (rate-limited, de-duped, and avoids high-cardinality payloads). Implementation notes: - Adds a new Alertmanager webhook handler for a small set of signals (lane_utilization_high, throttling_spike, router_admission_reject_spike) and normalizes them into a single IncidentSignal type. - Adds a Slack message renderer that produces a compact block + a short plain-text fallback, with stable fields for copy/paste into the incident doc. - Links: Dashboard: “Hot-route capacity protection” (grafana://dashboards/hot-route-protection) and Runbook: “Overload throttling and priority routing response” (confluence://oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/overload-throttling-and-priority-routing-response). - Adds de-dupe keyed by (incident_id, signal_type, route_bucket) with a 10-minute TTL to avoid spam during alert flaps. - Adds an explicit allowlist for labels we read from alerts; everything else is dropped to prevent surprise cardinality / data leakage. - Adds unit tests for formatting (including missing fields) and for de-dupe behavior. Testing: - Local: make test, make lint, make run; verified messages in #eng-sre-sandbox using a synthetic Alertmanager payload. - Verified that messages do not include tenant_id, customer_name, or full route strings (only route_bucket / hashed route id). Rollout: No special rollout; bot deploy happens via standard pipeline. This should be low risk: feature is gated behind HOT_ROUTE_LANE_SUMMARY_ENABLED=true and can be toggled at runtime via config reload.
commits: incidentbot: add IncidentSignal model and allowlisted alert parsing
slack: render lane health + throttling spike summary blocks
dedupe: cache + TTL for incident signal notifications
commands: add /lane-health responder command and help text
tests: formatting snapshots + dedupe behavior + redaction checks
files_changed: cmd/incident-bot/main.go (wire webhook + command routing; feature flag)
conversation:
Sean Gallagher (review): The message format looks good, but I want to make sure we don’t page-spam incident channels during load tests or alert flaps. What’s the de-dupe behavior and can we tune it quickly?
Rafael Mendes (author): Added de-dupe by (incident_id, signal_type, route_bucket) with 10m TTL (configurable via LANE_SUMMARY_DEDUPE_TTL). Also gated behind HOT_ROUTE_LANE_SUMMARY_ENABLED so we can disable instantly if it’s noisy.

Aisha Bello (review): Can we include direct links to (1) the hot-route protection dashboard and (2) the runbook section for verifying lane behavior? Also, please use stable link strings so we can swap targets later without code changes.
Rafael Mendes (author): Done. Added two config-backed links (LANE_HEALTH_DASHBOARD_URL and LANE_HEALTH_RUNBOOK_URL). Defaults point to the dashboard + runbook you referenced.

Sergio Costa (review): Observability/cost note: please avoid rendering per-route lists larger than N. Some incidents have dozens of routes. Also ensure we’re not passing through raw labels from Alertmanager that might include tenant metadata.
Rafael Mendes (author): Capped affected routes to top 5 by throttled_rate (from the alert payload’s aggregated fields). Implemented allowlist parsing: only reads route_bucket, tier, region, and a small fixed set of numeric fields; everything else discarded. Also added a test that fails if tenant_id/customer_name appears in the rendered message.

Sean Gallagher (follow-up): Nit: include guidance text for the common question: “Is this expected throttling or a bug?”
Rafael Mendes (author): Added a short line with next steps and runbook pointer: check lane utilization + admission rejects; if enterprise lane is rejecting >1% sustained, validate capacity dip and consider enabling stricter shedding for self-serve per runbook.
